Then Abaqa commanded his brother's son and his son-in-law
that they should be the judges,
and see which of the two sides was in the right.
And when they had been judging for about a month of days,
Papa (Baba?) was condemned,
and those first judges were exposed,
and they confessed to the bribe which they had received from Papa (Baba?).
And an order went out,
and the head of Papa (Baba?) was cut off with the sword on a Thursday (?), the eighth of the month of Ab of that same year of the Emir;
and it was brought to Mosul.
And again those Christian governors took authority over Mosul and Erbil,
and they triumphed greatly.
Moreover, also a great Persian man of high lineage,
whose name was Jalal al-Din Turan, from the country of Khotan,
was also killed on the charge that he used to take the side of Papa (Baba?),
and did not rebuke his insolence.
And in those days,
a certain Kurdish emir from the country of Mosul,
whose name was Badru,
fled to Syria with all his people.
Indeed, the road guards from the Tatar army pursued after him,
but they did not overtake him.
As for Sunqur al-Ashqar, however,
he who was in Damascus,
he would not submit to Alfi {Qalawun} that he should reign in Egypt,
but gathered an army and encountered him.
And when Alfi prevailed over him,
he fled from before him,
and came to Rahbuth to the Bedouin emir Isa,
and both of them agreed,
and sent an envoy to Abaqa, king of kings,
that he should send armies against Alfi.
And when he listened to them,
and the armies descended to Syria,
that Sunqur became afraid for his life on account of them,
and did not trust them,
but fled and took refuge in the fortress of Sahyun.
And the Tatars reached as far as Aleppo,
and devastated {OCR?} with the edge of the sword everyone who fell into their hands,
and burned {OCR?} the buildings and returned.
Now the majority of the people hid themselves in caves,
and were saved from the sword.
Now this descent of theirs into Syria took place in the days of winter,
in the year 1592
(1592 of the Greeks?),
while Qunghartai, the younger brother of Abaqa, king of kings, was standing at their head.
And after the Tatars had turned back from Aleppo,
seven thousand Egyptian horsemen assembled,
and went to camp against the fortress of Marqab
